memo: Member is 47, caring for a 15-year-old, claims caretaker exemption. CRITICAL: Caretaker exemption covers age 13 or younger only (chunk EX-CARETAKER: 'dependent child age 13 or younger'). The 15-year-old does not qualify. Member has reported zero hours and has no documents on hand. Screening shows 80-hour shortfall and no supported exemption. Deadline is 2026-07-24 (6.6 days remaining). Member appears to have stopped reporting entirely, believing an exemption applies that does not apply to a 15-year-old. Two paths exist but both require immediate action: (1) if member qualifies for a different exemption (disability, pregnancy, SSI/SSDI, recent incarceration, or foster care history), gather proof documents now; (2) if no other exemption applies, member must report qualifying hours (work, school, job training, community service—any combination totaling 80/month) with accepted proof by deadline. The gap between belief and rule, plus the imminent deadline and zero activity reporting, makes this a case where a navigator must clarify the rule in plain language and help the member identify what they have actually done in the past month.
member_impact:
Hello. We need to talk about your Medicaid renewal right away. You have until July 24 to send information — that is only 6 days away.

You said you are caring for your 15-year-old. That is important work. But the caretaker rule covers children age 13 and younger only. Your child is 15, so that rule does not apply to you.

This means you need to report 80 hours per month of other activities — like a job, school, volunteer work, or job training — and send proof of those hours. You have not reported any hours yet.

You have two options:

**Option 1:** Do you have any other reason you might be exempt? For example, are you on disability benefits (SSI or SSDI), age 65 or older, a former foster youth under 26, pregnant, or were you recently released from jail or prison? If yes, tell us now and bring proof.

**Option 2:** Did you do any work, school, volunteer, or training in the last month? If yes, we need to gather proof (pay stubs, school records, volunteer letters, etc.) and send it in right away.

Please call or come in today. We cannot wait until July 24.
missing_documents: Proof of any qualifying activities (work, school, job training, community service) — at least 80 hours per month
OR proof of a different exemption (disability benefit award letter, birth certificate showing age 65+, foster-care documentation, pregnancy provider statement, incarceration release letter)
recommended_actions: Contact member immediately to clarify that caretaker exemption applies only to children age 13 or younger; the 15-year-old does not qualify.
Ask member about other possible exemptions: disability benefits (SSI/SSDI), age 65+, former foster youth under 26, pregnancy, recent incarceration release.

If no other exemption applies: ask member to detail all activities in the past month (employment, education, training, volunteering). Collect proof documents (pay stubs, school enrollment, volunteer letters, training certificates).
With proof in hand, submit response on behalf of member before 2026-07-24T23:59:00 to avoid non-compliance termination and loss of the 30-day cure window.
If deadline is missed, remind member of the 30-day cure window (after non-compliance notice) and 90-day reconsideration window (after termination).

citations.quote: A parent, guardian, or caretaker relative of a dependent child age 13 or younger is exempt
Adults age 19 to 64 covered through Medicaid expansion must complete at least 80 hours per month of qualifying activities, unless an exemption applies
Before coverage is ended for not meeting the community-engagement requirement, the state must send a non-compliance notice, and the person has 30 days to demonstrate compliance or an exemption
If coverage is terminated for a procedural reason — missing paperwork, an unanswered notice — there is a 90-day reconsideration period after the termination date

findings.detail: Only 7 days remain to respond (due 2026-07-24T23:59:00). If more time is genuinely needed, the 30-day cure window after a non-compliance notice is a safety net — but do not plan on it.
The member believes the 'caretaker_young_child' exemption applies, but the facts on file do not show it. Do not rely on it without a navigator confirming — plan for the hours path in parallel.

Qualifying hours: 0 per month (none reported) — 80 hours SHORT of the 80-hour standard. Close the gap with any qualifying mix (work, school, job training, community service) or confirm an exemption before relying on hours.
Every claimed activity (0) has an accepted document on hand.
